reader_summary.headline: This is the memo by Howard Marks, Ruminating on Assets Allocation.
reader_summary.overview: This is the memo by Howard Marks, Ruminating on Assets Allocation. When I travel to see clients and spend entire days discussing investing and the markets, memo ideas often pop up. Last month's visit with clients in Australia is a case in point.

key_points.text: We talked about the sea change, I believe, is taking place in interest rates, and about the role of credit in portfolios.
key_points.evidence_quote: We talked about the sea change, I believe, is taking place in interest rates, and about the role of credit in portfolios.

key_points.text: And in a few cases, this led to the general topic of asset allocation.
key_points.evidence_quote: And in a few cases, this led to the general topic of asset allocation.

key_points.text: a lot of new ideas on the subject, but rather a new way to combine old ideas into a unified theory.

key_points.text: Before I proceed, I want to mention that from time to time in this memo, I'll say generally, usually, or everything else being equal.

highlights.text:
Insistence on preserving capital, or, secondarily, on limiting the portfolio's volatility,
calls for an emphasis on defense, which precludes pursuing maximum growth.

Insistence on preserving capital, or, secondarily, on limiting the portfolio's volatility,
calls for an emphasis on defense, which precludes pursuing maximum growth.

highlights.text:
Correspondingly, a decision to strive to maximize growth requires an emphasis on offense,
meaning preservation of capital and steadiness must be sacrificed to some degree.

and maximization of growth, or defense and offense.
